많은 일하는 어머니들은 "엄마 죄책감"으로 알려진 것을 경험합니다. 이것은 일과 가족 책임의 균형을 맞추려고 노력하는 데서 오는 죄책감이나 불안감입니다. 일하는 어머니는 자녀와 충분한 시간을 보내지 않거나 중요한 이정표를 놓치거나 학교 행사에 참석할 수 없는 것에 대해 죄책감을 느낄 수 있습니다.

Introduction

While working mothers face many challenges, there are also many benefits to being a working mom. In this chapter, we will explore the positive impact that working mothers can have on their personal and family life, as well as the benefits they can experience at work.

Positive Impact on Personal and Family Life

1. Financial independence: One of the most significant benefits of being a working mom is the financial independence that comes with having a steady income. This can provide greater stability for the family and allow working mothers to invest in their children's education and future.
2. Role modeling: Working mothers can be powerful role models for their children, showing them the value of hard work and the importance of pursuing their passions. This can inspire children to pursue their own goals and dreams.
3. Increased confidence: By juggling work and family responsibilities, working mothers can develop greater self-confidence and self-esteem. They learn to trust their abilities and take on new challenges, both at home and in the workplace.
4. Social connections: Working mothers have the opportunity to build social connections and friendships outside of the home. This can provide a sense of community and support that can be valuable for both mothers and their families.

Benefits at Work

1. Career advancement: Working mothers who are dedicated to their careers and work hard to balance their responsibilities can achieve career advancement and greater job satisfaction. This can lead to higher salaries and greater opportunities for growth and development.
2. Improved time management and multitasking skills: Working mothers learn to manage their time effectively, prioritize tasks, and multitask. These skills can be valuable in the workplace and in other areas of life.
3. Greater creativity and innovation: Working mothers bring unique perspectives and experiences to the workplace, which can lead to greater creativity and innovation. They may also be more adept at problem-solving and finding new solutions.

Improve Your Time Management and Multitasking Skills

One of the most significant benefits of being a working mom is the development of time management and multitasking skills. Here are some tips for improving these skills:

1. Prioritize tasks: Make a to-do list each day and prioritize the most important tasks. Focus on completing these tasks first, and then move on to less urgent items.
2. Use a calendar: Use a calendar to schedule appointments, meetings, and deadlines. This can help you stay organized and on track.
3. Learn to say no: Don't take on too much at once. Learn to say no to non-essential tasks or delegate them to others.
4. Take breaks: Take regular breaks throughout the day to recharge and refocus. This can help you stay productive and avoid burnout.

Behind the Scenes of a Science Working Mom

Gender roles and stereotypes can also have an impact on the experiences of working mothers. Mothers may face social pressure to prioritize their children over their careers or may be viewed as less committed to their jobs. Employers and society as a whole can help to combat these stereotypes by offering support and resources for working mothers.

Psychological and Social Benefits of Working Mothers

Working mothers can experience a range of psychological and social benefits, including:

1. Greater sense of purpose: Working mothers may feel a greater sense of purpose and fulfillment from both their family and work lives.
2. Reduced stress: Studies have shown that working mothers may experience less stress than stay-at-home mothers, as they have a sense of autonomy and control over their lives

La construction du poster de présentation du PTUT

La forme
• Un format standard A0 (84,1 cm \* 118,9 cm).
• Une orientation paysage ou portrait
• Une taille de polices normée : 
o 59 à 64 pts pour le titre du poster
o 38 à 42 pts pour les noms d'auteurs et l'adresse des auteurs
o environ 40 pts pour les titres niveau 1
o 24 pts minimum pour le corps du texte
• Une marge de 2,5 cm sur tout le pourtour du poster
• Règle de composition : 30 % texte, 30 % blanc, 40 % de figures graphiques
• Veiller au contraste : si le fond est foncé, utiliser une police d’écriture claire et inversement
• Harmoniser l’ensemble (couleur, forme, police)

Le contenu
• Le titre
• Le nom des auteurs, leur affiliation, le sigle de l'université, la date
• L’introduction : le contexte / l'objectif présenté de manière synthétique
• le matériel et les méthodes (le nombre de personnes, la qualification ou les compétences, les outils, les innovations, les étapes dans la gestion du projet)
• Les résultats mis en valeur
• La conclusion (les applications et les perspectives)
• Les remerciements et les logos avec la mention des partenaires 
• Le ou les contacts
• Les sources / les partenaires le cas échéant
• Rédiger des phrases courtes.
• Son contenu doit être facilement accessible même pour un lecteur autonome. Il est donc nécessaire d’adopter une stratégie de communication attractive, structurée et concise.
Le titre
Le titre doit interpeler, informer et annoncer.
Il peut :
• Être direct 
Ex : Chat GPT, les nouveaux enjeux de l’intelligence artificielle
• Exposer un conflit
Ex : Intelligence artificielle : cauchemar ou révolution ?
• Poser une question 
Ex : Incidence et risque des nouveaux usages de l'intelligence artificielle - de quoi Chat GPT est-il le nom ?
• Présenter un jeu de mots 
Ex : Donner sa langue au Chat GPT
Un bon titre, c’est quoi ?
• Facile à mémoriser
• Valable pour un seul poster
• Ne heurte pas le lecteur
Le contenu textuel
• Les effets artistiques ne remplacent pas un bon contenu
• Les informations partagées doivent être pertinentes et précises.
• L’introduction est le fil conducteur. Elle est composée d’environ 25 mots définissant le comment, le pourquoi, et le message principal du poster. Chaque partie du poster doit se rattacher au fil conducteur
• Les parties « méthodes et résultats » doivent représenter les 2/3 du poster
• Faire preuve d’esprit de synthèse : le volume de texte n’excède pas 1/3 de la surface
• Utiliser des phrases courtes
• Privilégier la forme impersonnelle et la voie passive
• Omettre les informations inutiles

Les figures graphiques
Elles doivent pouvoir à elles seules transmettre un message. 
La figure graphique ne doit pas être une illustration mais une contribution à la compréhension
Pour cela, on veille à leur qualité :
• Valeur informative / pertinence
• Clarté des données
• Disponibilité / droits d’auteur

Bienvenue à l'IUT de Clermont-Ferrand, site du Puy-en-Velay, département Informatique Graphique pour l'année académique 2022-2023. Nous sommes fiers de présenter un projet tuteuré de deuxième année passionnant en collaboration avec le musée de l'aire et de l'espace de Paris le Bourget. Ce projet consiste en la conception et le développement d'une scène de jeu de combat d'avion en réalité virtuelle (VR), basé sur le régiment de chasse 2/30 "Normandie-Niémen" durant la Seconde Guerre mondiale.

Notre projet vise à offrir une expérience immersive aux utilisateurs en les mettant dans la peau des aviateurs français qui ont combattu aux côtés de l'Armée rouge sur le sol soviétique. Le projet est dirigé par Isabelle Portail et implique plusieurs secteurs de travail, notamment les designers, les programmeurs, les level designers et les artistes en création/animation 3D. Chaque membre travaillera sur un aspect différent du jeu, allant de la conceptualisation de l'expérience de l'utilisateur et du concept de jeu, à la modélisation, la création de textures et d'effets spéciaux, l'animation et la mise en place des éléments de gameplay.

Nous espérons que le jeu sera suffisamment avancé pour être présenté et joué au musée de l'aire et de l'espace de Paris le Bourget, où nous aurons également l'opportunité de rencontrer le responsable de l'espace "Normandie-Niemen" et de visiter le musée. Ce projet sera un excellent moyen pour les étudiants de développer leurs compétences et d'acquérir une expérience pratique dans le domaine de la création de jeux en VR.

## Bölüm Özeti

\* Hocanın konu anlatımı burada \*
Sosyolojiye giriş dersine hoş geldiniz. Bu ilk dersimizde sizlerle, kısaca bilim olarak sosyoloji, sosyolojinin temel kavramları ve sosyoloji diğer sosyal bilimleri ilişkiler üzerinde duracağız. Hiç merak ettiniz mi günümüzün gençliğiyle onların anne babalarının değerleri arasındaki farkları ya da şunlar hakkında hiç düşündünüz mü? Neden günümüzdeki aile yapısı geçmişten farklıdır veya toplumda neden kadınlar ikinci plandadır, geri plandadır veya birçok toplumda boşanmalar giderek artıyor, bizde de artıyor. Neden boşanmalar artıyor veya aşk evlilikleri geliniksel toplumlarda neden yaygın değildi? Bu ve buna benzer her gün yüzlerce soru soruyoruz. Aslında bu sorular sormaya başladığınızda amatör sosyoloji yapmaya başladığınız demektir. Sosyoloji latince birliktelik anlamına gelen socuyu sözcüyle, Yunanca İnceleme Stadi ya da çalışma anlamına gelen logos sözcüklerinin bir araya getirilmesinden oluşmaktadır. Kelime anlamıyla sosyoloji toplumsal üyeliğin temellerinin incelenmesini ifade etmektedir. Sosyolojinin isim babası Ogus Comptdur ve sosyoloji için ilk kullandığı sözcük, ilk ürettiği sözcük sosyal fiziktir. Daha sonra Compt sosyal fizik ifadesini kavramına terk etmiş onun yerine sosyoloji sözcüğünü ifade etmiştir. Sosyolojinin çok farklı tanımları var. Ortak noktaları da var elbette bu tanımların. Dür kayma göre sosyoloji toplumsal kurumları incelenen bilim dalıdır. Bir başka sosyoloji göre toplumsal fenomenleri ve bere göre toplumsal eylemi simese göre insan ilişkilerini incelenen bilim dalıdır. En genel tanımlarından birisi sosyolojinin insan toplumunun sistematik ve belli bir kuşku ve belli bir metod içerisinde incelenmesini ifade etmektedir. Bir sosyoluk günümüzde güreşin altındaki her şeyin sosyolojisi olduğunu söylüyor. Yani bugün artık iktisadın sosyolojisi var, siyasetin sosyolojisi var, hukukun sosyolojisi var. Aklınıza gelecek kültürün vesaire aşkın her şeyin sosyolojisi var. İki insan bir araya geldiği zaman orada bir toplumsal ilişki başlıyor ve 10 noktadan sonra bir takım sosyolojik analizleri yapmanız mümkün hale geliyor. Bir sosyoloj diyor ki sosyoloji bize içinde yaşadığımız topluma uzaylı yaratıklar gibi bakma becerisi kazandırır. İlk anda bu sinir bozucu bir sözcük olarak gelebilir size. Ama biz içinde yaşadığımız toplumun dışına çıkmadığımız müddetçe bazı şeyleri kavramamız zorlaşmaktadır. Çünkü sürekli aynı toplumun içinde yaşayan insanlar bir süre sonra o yaşadıkları deneyimlere alışmakta ve onun üzerine düşünmemektedirler. Dolayısıyla bir anlamda sosyoloji alışık olduğumuz perspektifin dışına çıkmaktadır. Dolayısıyla bunun bir rahatsız hepçisi edici tarafı da söz konusudur. Dolayısıyla sosyolojik perspektif bir dünyaya farklı bakış açısı sunmaktadır. Ve tabii farklı dünyalar arasında sosyoloji yeni pencereler açmaktadır. Bir diğer ifadeyle sosyoloji içinde yaşadığımız dünyayı daha geniş bir bağlamda görme imkanı sağlamaktadır. Kemen sorularından bir tanesi insanların toplum tarafından nasıl etkilendiydir? Bir diğer ifadeyle sosyolojik hayal gücü içinde yaşadığımız toplum ve kendimiz arasındaki ilişkiyi görme imkanı sağlar. Eğer biz içinde yaşadığımız toplumu iyi anlayamazsak aslında kendimizi anlamamız da çok kolay değildir. Çünkü biz insanlar bir taraftan toplumu toplumsal ilişkileri biçimlendirirken diğer taraftan toplumsal toplum ve toplumlu toplumsal ilişkiler tarafından biçimlendirilen varlıklarız. Rite-Messi söylediği gibi sosyoloji tarih ile biyografi arasındaki ilişkiyi daha iyi kavramamıza yardımcı oluyor. Ve bizler açısından toplumun ve içinde yaşadığımız tarihsel süreçlerin bir ürünü olduğumuzu fark etmemizi sağlıyor. Biz toplumu ve birey birlikte anlamadıkça ne bireyin hayatını ne de tarihi tam olarak kavramamız söz konusu değildiyor. Dur kayma göre toplum bireylerin basit bir toplamı değildir. Onun için toplum kendine has nitelikleri olan özgül bir gerçekliği temsil etmektedir. Tabi belki toplumu bir cümle ile tanımlamak gerekebilir. O da şu anlama geliyor toplum dediğimiz şey burada bir kültür ve bölgeyi paylaşan insan grubunu kastediyoruz. Bir başka tanımda da toplumu ortak kültürü paylaşan belli bir toplak toprak parçası üzerinde yerleşik, kendilerini birleşik ve özgün varlık olarak gören insanlardan oluşan bir grup olarak tanımlamak mümkündür. Sosyoloji'nin kuşkusuz en önemli isimlerinden birisi kurcubabalarından birisi de Max Weber'dır. Weber'e göre sosyoloji toplumsal davranışı ya da toplumsal eğlemi inceleyen bilim dalının adıdır. Weber toplumsal eğlemi dört grupta sınıflıyor. Bunlardan birincisi amaçla ilgili toplumsal eğlen, diğeri değerle ilişkili toplumsal eğlen, bir başkası duygusal eğlen ya da duygusal davranış son olarak da geleneksel davranış şeklinde bir sınıflanmaya tabi tutuyor. Weber amaçla ilgili rasyonel davranışı anlatırken şunu kastediyor. Diyor ki insanların belli amaçları var. Bu amaçlara ulaşabilmek için belli hesap kitaplar yaparlar. Bu çerçevede kendileri için en az maliyetle, en kazançlı olanı gerçekleştirmeye çalışırlar. Bu konuda verdiği örneklerden birisi amacı yönelik rasyonel davranışa ilişkin verdiği örneklerden birisi köprü yapan mühendisin davranışıdır. İkinci davranış biçimi, değeri ilişkin rasyonel davranışı idi. Burada da belli bir rasyonellik var ama bu amacı yönelik rasyonel davranıştan farklıdır. Örneğin gemisiyle batan kaptanın davranışı aslında değeri yönelik rasyonel davranıştır. Yani görülür de kaptanın kendisiyle kurtarması lazım fakat orada bir kaptanın en önemli değerlerinden birisi, gemiyi kaptanın terk etmeyeceği ise, gemisiyle sahip çıkması gerektiği ise bu bir tür değerden kaynaklanan rasyonelteyi ifade eder. Duygusal davranış dediğimiz şey rasyonel davranışın aslında biraz karşısındaki bir davranış biçimi. Rasyonel davranış hesaplı, kitaplı, kontrolülü amaç odaklı bir davranış olmasına karşılık. Duygusal davranış sonuçlarını hesap etmeden kişinin duygularına kapılarak yaptığı davranışa duygusal davranış diyoruz. Örneğin alayın çocuğa tokat vuran annenin davranışını düşündüğünüzde aslında bu bir tür duygusal davranış olarak ifade edebileceğimiz davranış biçimidir. Çünkü alayan çocuğa siz tokat vuruyorsanız bu çocuğun susması mümkün değildir, daha çok ağlayacaktır. Ama orada arnaya artık bunu almıştır ve dolayısıyla ister istemez duygularına kapılıp böyle bir tepki gösterebilir. Gelimeksel davranış ise içinde yaşadığımız geleneklerin bize zorladığı davranış biçimidir. Yani yüzlerce yıldır insanlar belli toprağı belli şekillerde ekip biçiyorlardır, belli şekillerde ilişki kuruyorlardır. Birbirlerine karşı baba oğul da oğul babaya ya da anne çocuğa, çocuk anneye karşı ya da büyüklerle küçükler arasında belli ilişki biçimi vardır. Bu ilişki biçimi yüzlerce yıldır artık alışkanlık ve gelene kalene gelmiştir ve bizim davranışlarımızın temel kaynağı burada artık o yüzlerce yıldır süren gelenektir. Bu birey ve toplum konusu sosyal ve biçok alanda çok tartışılan konulardan birisidir. Bir zamanlar İngiltere'nin başbakanlığını yapan Margaret Thatcher'ın bir sözü vardı, çok tartışılan şöyle diyordu Thatcher, toplum diye bir şey yoktur diyordu, sadece bireyler kadınlar ve erkekler vardır. Gerçekten de Thatcher'ın dediği gibi toplum diye bir şey yok mu, sadece kadınlar ve erkekler mi var, eğer toplum diye bir şey yoksa o zaman sosyolojiye ne gerek var? Bu elbette sosyolojik perspektif içerisinde kabul edilebilecek bir söz değil. Sosyolojik hayal gücünü açıklarken Wright Bills şunu söylüyor, bizim diyor bireysel gibi gördüğümüz bir çok sorunun aslında toplumsal bir temeli vardır. Örneğin işlerimizi iyi gittiği zamanlarda hepimiz kendi başarılarımıza çok fırgı yaparız. Sürekli övünürüz, şunları başardık, bunları gerçekleştirdik vesaire diye. Ve bunları hep sorarlarsa kendimizin yaptığını söyleriz. Bunları bizim başarımız olarak sunarız. Ama gün gelir büyük bir ekonomik kriz ortaya çıkar, kazançlarımızın hepsi yok olur gider. Sonra anlarız ki hepimiz aslında toplumun bize sunduğu imkanlar kadar belli şeyleri başarabiliyoruz. "Data Fetching Fundamentals
The Next.js App Router introduces a new, simplified data fetching system built on React and the Web platform. This page will go through the fundamental concepts and patterns to help you manage your data's lifecycle.

Good to know: Previous Next.js data fetching methods such as getServerSideProps, getStaticProps, and getInitialProps are not supported in the new app directory.

Overview
Here's a quick overview of the recommendations on this page:

Fetch data on the server using Server Components.
Fetch data in parallel to minimize waterfalls and reduce loading times.
For Layouts and Pages, fetch data where it's used. Next.js will automatically dedupe requests in a tree.
Use Loading UI, Streaming and Suspense to progressively render a page and show a result to the user while the rest of the content loads.
The fetch() API
The new data fetching system is built on top of the native fetch() Web API and makes use of async/await in Server Components.

React extends fetch to provide automatic request deduping.
Next.js extends the fetch options object to allow each request to set its own caching and revalidating rules.
Learn how to use fetch in Next.js.

Fetching Data on the Server
Whenever possible, we recommend fetching data inside Server Components. Server Components always fetch data on the server. This allows you to:

Have direct access to backend data resources (e.g. databases).
Keep your application more secure by preventing sensitive information, such as access tokens and API keys, from being exposed to the client.
Fetch data and render in the same environment. This reduces both the back-and-forth communication between client and server, as well as the work on the main thread on the client.
Perform multiple data fetches with single round-trip instead of multiple individual requests on the client.
Reduce client-server waterfalls.
Depending on your region, data fetching can also happen closer to your data source, reducing latency and improving performance.
Learn more about Client and Server Components.

Good to know: It's still possible to fetch data client-side. We recommend using a third-party library such as SWR or React Query with Client components. In the future, it'll also be possible to fetch data in Client Components using React's use() hook.

Component-level Data Fetching
In this new model, you can fetch data inside layouts, pages, and components. Data fetching is also compatible with Streaming and Suspense.

Good to know: For layouts, it's not possible to pass data between a parent layout and its children. We recommend fetching data directly inside the layout that needs it, even if you're requesting the same data multiple times in a route. Behind the scenes, React and Next.js will cache and dedupe requests to avoid the same data being fetched more than once.

Parallel and Sequential Data Fetching
When fetching data inside components, you need to be aware of two data fetching patterns: Parallel and Sequential.

Server and Client Components
With parallel data fetching, requests in a route are eagerly initiated and will load data at the same time. This reduces client-server waterfalls and the total time it takes to load data.
With sequential data fetching, requests in a route are dependent on each other and create waterfalls. There may be cases where you want this pattern because one fetch depends on the result of the other, or you want a condition to be satisfied before the next fetch to save resources. However, this behavior can also be unintentional and lead to longer loading times.
Learn how to implement parallel and sequential data fetching.

Automatic fetch() Request Deduping
If you need to fetch the same data (e.g. current user) in multiple components in a tree, Next.js will automatically cache fetch requests (GET) that have the same input in a temporary cache. This optimization prevents the same data from being fetched more than once during a rendering pass.

Deduplication in a component tree
On the server, the cache lasts the lifetime of a server request until the rendering process completes.
This optimization applies to fetch requests made in Layouts, Pages, Server Components, generateMetadata and generateStaticParams.
This optimization also applies during static generation.
On the client, the cache lasts the duration of a session (which could include multiple client-side re-renders) before a full page reload.
Good to know:

POST requests are not automatically deduplicated. Learn more about caching.
If you're unable to use fetch, React provides a cache function to allow you to manually cache data for the duration of the request.
Static and Dynamic Data Fetches
There are two types of data: Static and Dynamic.

Static Data is data that doesn't change often. For example, a blog post.
Dynamic Data is data that changes often or can be specific to users. For example, a shopping cart list.
Dynamic and Static Data Fetching
By default, Next.js automatically does static fetches. This means that the data will be fetched at build time, cached, and reused on each request. As a developer, you have control over how the static data is cached and revalidated.

There are two benefits to using static data:

It reduces the load on your database by minimizing the number of requests made.
The data is automatically cached for improved loading performance.
However, if your data is personalized to the user or you want to always fetch the latest data, you can mark requests as dynamic and fetch data on each request without caching.

Learn how to do Static and Dynamic data fetching.

Caching Data
Caching is the process of storing data in a location (e.g. Content Delivery Network) so doesn't need to be re-fetched from the original source on each request.

Static Site Generation with Caching
The Next.js Cache is a persistent HTTP cache that can be globally distributed. This means the cache can scale automatically and be shared across multiple regions depending on your platform (e.g. Vercel).

Next.js extends the options object of the fetch() function to allow each request on the server to set its own persistent caching behavior. Together with component-level data fetching, this allows you to configure caching within your application code directly where the data is being used.

During server rendering, when Next.js comes across a fetch, it will check the cache to see if the data is already available. If it is, it will return the cached data. If not, it will fetch and store data for future requests.

Good to know: If you're unable to use fetch, React provides a cache function to allow you to manually cache data for the duration of the request.

Learn more about caching in Next.js.

Revalidating Data
Revalidation is the process of purging the cache and re-fetching the latest data. This is useful when your data changes and you want to ensure your application shows the latest version without having to rebuild your entire application.

Next.js provides two types of revalidation:

Background: Revalidates the data at a specific time interval.
On-demand: Revalidates the data whenever there is an update.
Learn how to revalidate data.

Streaming and Suspense
Streaming and Suspense are new React features that allow you to progressively render and incrementally stream rendered units of the UI to the client.

With Server Components and nested layouts, you're able to instantly render parts of the page that do not specifically require data, and show a loading state for parts of the page that are fetching data. This means the user does not have to wait for the entire page to load before they can start interacting with it.

Server Rendering with Streaming
To learn more about Streaming and Suspense, see the Loading UI and Streaming and Suspense pages.

Routing Fundamentals
Next.js 13 introduced the new App Router built on top of React Server Components with support for layouts, nested routing, loading states, error handling, and more.

This page will introduce you to the fundamental concepts of the new routing model.

Terminology
You will see these terms being used throughout the documentation. Here's a quick reference:

A tree of folders with a subtree, root, and leaves
Tree: A convention for visualizing a hierarchical structure. For example, a component tree with parent and children components, a folder structure, etc.
Subtree: Part of a tree, starting at a new root (first) and ending at the leaves (last).
Root: The first node in a tree or subtree, such as a root layout.
Leaf: Nodes in a subtree that have no children, such as the last segment in a URL path.
Anatomy of a URL
URL Segment: Part of the URL path delimited by slashes.
URL Path: Part of the URL that comes after the domain (composed of segments).
The app Directory
The new App Router works in a new directory named app. The app directory works alongside the pages directory to allow for incremental adoption. This allows you to opt some routes of your application into the new behavior while keeping other routes in the pages directory for previous behavior.

Good to know: Routes across directories should not resolve to the same URL path and will cause a build-time error to prevent a conflict.

The new app directory with folders as routes
By default, components inside app are React Server Components. This is a performance optimization and allows you to easily adopt them. However, you can also use Client Components.

Recommendation: Check out the Server and Client Components page if you're new to Server Components.

Folders and Files inside app
In the app directory:

Folders are used to define routes. A route is a single path of nested folders, following the hierarchy from the root folder down to a final leaf folder that includes a page.js file.
Files are used to create UI that is shown for the route segment. See special files.
Route Segments
Each folder in a route represents a route segment. Each route segment is mapped to a corresponding segment in a URL path.

Route segments mapping to URL segments
Nested Routes
To create a nested route, you can nest folders inside each other. For example, you can add a new /dashboard/settings route by nesting two new folders in the app directory.

The /dashboard/settings route is composed of three segments:

/ (Root segment)
dashboard (Segment)
settings (Leaf segment)
File Conventions
Next.js provides a set of special files to create UI with specific behavior in nested routes:

page.js: Create the unique UI of a route and make the path publicly accessible.
route.js: Create server-side API endpoints for a route (available in next@canary).
layout.js: Create shared UI for a segment and its children. A layout wraps a page or child segment.
template.js: Similar to layout.js, except a new component instance is mounted on navigation. Use layouts unless you need this behavior.
loading.js: Create loading UI for a segment and its children. loading.js wraps a page or child segment in a React Suspense Boundary, showing the loading UI while they load.
error.js: Create error UI for a segment and its children. error.js wraps a page or child segment in a React Error Boundary, showing the error UI if an error is caught.
global-error.js: Similar to error.js, but specifically for catching errors in the root layout.js.
not-found.js: Create UI to show when the notFound function is thrown within a route segment.
Good to know: .js, .jsx, or .tsx file extensions can be used for special files.

Component Hierarchy
The React components defined in special files of a route segment are rendered in a specific hierarchy:

layout.js
template.js
error.js (React error boundary)
loading.js (React suspense boundary)
not-found.js (React error boundary)
page.js or nested layout.js
Rendered component hierarchy
In a nested route, the components of a segment will be nested inside the components of its parent segment.

Nested rendered component hierarchy
Colocation
In addition to special files, you have the option to colocate your own files inside folders. For example, stylesheets, tests, components, and more.

An example folder of colocated files
Server-Centric Routing with Client-side Navigation
Unlike the pages directory which uses client-side routing, the new router in the app directory uses server-centric routing to align with Server Components and data fetching on the server. With server-centric routing, the client does not have to download a route map and the same request for Server Components can be used to look up routes. This optimization is useful for all applications, but has a larger impact on applications with many routes.

Although routing is server-centric, the router uses client-side navigation with the Link Component - resembling the behavior of a Single-Page Application. This means when a user navigates to a new route, the browser will not reload the page. Instead, the URL will be updated and Next.js will only render the segments that change.

Additionally, as users navigate around the app, the router will store the result of the React Server Component payload in an in-memory client-side cache. The cache is split by route segments which allows invalidation at any level and ensures consistency across concurrent renders. This means that for certain cases, the cache of a previously fetched segment can be re-used, further improving performance.

Checkout the Linking and Navigating page to learn how to use the Link component.

Partial Rendering
When navigating between sibling routes (e.g. /dashboard/settings and /dashboard/analytics below), Next.js will only fetch and render the layouts and pages in routes that change. It will not re-fetch or re-render anything above the segments in the subtree. This means that in routes that share a layout, the layout will be preserved when a user navigates between sibling pages.

Partial Rendering
Without partial rendering, each navigation would cause the full page to re-render on the server. Rendering only the segment that’s updating reduces the amount of data transferred and execution time, leading to improved performance.

Advanced Routing Patterns
In the future, the Next.js Router will provide a set of conventions to help you implement more advanced routing patterns. These include:

Parallel Routes: Allow you to simultaneously show two or more pages in the same view that can be navigated independently. You can use them for split views that have their own sub-navigation. E.g. Dashboards.
Intercepting Routes: Allow you to intercept a route and show it in the context of another route. You can use these when keeping the context for the current page is important. E.g. Seeing all tasks while editing one task or expanding a photo in a feed.
Conditional Routes: Allow you to conditionally render a route based on a condition. E.g. Showing a page only if the user is logged in.
These patterns and conventions will allow you to build richer, more complex UIs in your Next.js applications.

Advanced routing patterns, such as parallel routes, intercepting routes, and conditional routes, will be available in the future to create richer and more complex UIs in Next.js applications.

Defining Routes
We recommend reading the Routing Fundamentals page before continuing.

This page will guide you through how to define and organize routes in your Next.js application.

Creating Routes
Inside the app directory, folders are used to define routes.

Each folder represents a route segment that maps to a URL segment. To create a nested route, you can nest folders inside each other.

Folders map to URL Segments
A special page.js file is used to make route segments publicly accessible.

Page files make route segments publicly accessible
In this example, the /dashboard/analytics URL path is not publicly accessible because it does not have a corresponding page.js file. This folder could be used to store components, stylesheets, images, or other colocated files.

Good to know: .js, .jsx, or .tsx file extensions can be used for special files.

Creating UI
Special file conventions are used to create UI for each route segment. The most common are pages to show UI unique to a route, and layouts to show UI that is shared across multiple routes.

For example, to create your first page, add a page.js file inside the app directory and export a React component:

app/page.js
export default function Page() {
 return Hello, Next.js!
===============

;
}
Learn more about creating pages and layouts.

Route Groups
The hierarchy of the app folder maps directly to URL paths. However, it’s possible to break out of this pattern by creating a route group. Route groups can be used to:

Organize routes without affecting the URL structure.
Opting-in specific route segments into a layout.
Create multiple root layouts by splitting your application.
Convention
A route group can be created by wrapping a folder’s name in parenthesis: (folderName)

Example: Organize routes without affecting the URL path
To organize routes without affecting the URL, create a group to keep related routes together. The folders in parenthesis will be omitted from the URL (e.g. (marketing) or (shop)).

Organizing routes without affecting the URL path
Even though routes inside (marketing) and (shop) share the same URL hierarchy, you can create a different layout for each group by adding a layout.js file inside their folders.

Multiple layouts in the same hierarchy
Example: Opting specific segments into a layout
To opt specific routes into a layout, create a new route group (e.g. (shop)) and move the routes that share the same layout into the group (e.g. account and cart). The routes outside of the group will not share the layout (e.g. checkout).

Opting into a Layout
Example: Creating multiple root layouts
To create multiple root layouts, remove the top-level layout.js file, and add a layout.js file inside each route groups. This is useful for partitioning an application into sections that have a completely different UI or experience. The and tags need to be added to each root layout.

Creating multiple root layouts
In the example above, both (marketing) and (shop) have their own root layout.

Good to know
The naming of route groups has no special significance other than for organization. They do not affect the URL path.
Routes inside route groups should not resolve to the same URL path. For example, since route groups don't affect URL structure, (marketing)/about/page.js and (shop)/about/page.js would both resolve to /about and cause an error.
Navigating across multiple root layouts will cause a full page load (as opposed to a client-side navigation). For example, navigating from /cart that uses app/(shop)/layout.js to /blog that uses app/(marketing)/layout.js will cause a full page load. This only applies to multiple root layouts.
Dynamic Segments
When you don't know the exact segment names ahead of time and want to create routes from dynamic data, you can use Dynamic Segments that are filled in at request time or prerendered at build time.

Convention
A Dynamic Segment can be created by wrapping a folder’s name in square brackets: [folderName]. For example, [id] or [slug].

Dynamic Segments are passed as the params prop to layout, page, route, and generateMetadata functions.

Example
For example, a simple blog could include the following route app/blog/[slug]/page.js where [slug] is the Dynamic Segment for blog posts.

app/blog/[slug]/page.js
export default function Page({ params }) {
 return My Post;
}
Route Example URL params
app/blog/[slug]/page.js /blog/a { slug: 'a' }
app/blog/[slug]/page.js /blog/b { slug: 'b' }
app/blog/[slug]/page.js /blog/c { slug: 'c' }
See the generateStaticParams() page to learn how to generate the params for the segment.

Note: Dynamic Segments are equivalent to Dynamic Routes in the pages directory.

Catch-all Segments
Dynamic Segments can be extended to catch-all subsequent segments by adding an ellipsis inside the brackets [...folderName].

For example, app/shop/[...slug]/page.js will match /shop/clothes, but also /shop/clothes/tops, /shop/clothes/tops/t-shirts, and so on.

Route Example URL params
app/shop/[...slug]/page.js /shop/a { slug: ['a'] }
app/shop/[...slug]/page.js /shop/a/b { slug: ['a', 'b'] }
app/shop/[...slug]/page.js /shop/a/b/c { slug: ['a', 'b', 'c'] }
Optional Catch-all Segments
Catch-all Segments can be made optional by including the parameter in double square brackets: [[...folderName]].

For example, app/shop/[[...slug]]/page.js will also match /shop, in addition to /shop/clothes, /shop/clothes/tops, /shop/clothes/tops/t-shirts.

The difference between catch-all and optional catch-all segments is that with optional, the route without the parameter is also matched (/shop in the example above).

Route Example URL params
app/shop/[[...slug]]/page.js /shop {}
app/shop/[[...slug]]/page.js /shop/a { slug: ['a'] }
app/shop/[[...slug]]/page.js /shop/a/b { slug: ['a', 'b'] }
app/shop/[[...slug]]/page.js /shop/a/b/c { slug: ['a', 'b', 'c'] }
TypeScript
When using TypeScript, you can add types for params depending on your configured route segment.

app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx
export default function Page({
 params,
}: {
 params: { slug: string };
}) {
 return My Page

Nested routes can be created by nesting folders inside each other. Special file conventions, such as page.js and layout.js, are used to create UI for each route segment.

Route groups can be utilized to organize routes without affecting the URL structure, opt specific route segments into a layout, or create multiple root layouts by splitting your application. Route groups are created by wrapping a folder's name in parentheses, like (folderName).

Dynamic segments can be employed when you don't know the exact segment names ahead of time and want to create routes from dynamic data. Dynamic segments are created by wrapping a folder's name in square brackets, like [folderName].

Catch-all segments can be used to match all subsequent segments by adding an ellipsis inside the brackets, like [...folderName]. Optional catch-all segments can be created by including the parameter in double square brackets, like [[...folderName]].

Pages and Layouts
We recommend reading the Routing Fundamentals and Defining Routes pages before continuing.

The App Router inside Next.js 13 introduced new file conventions to easily create pages, shared layouts, and templates. This page will guide you through how to use these special files in your Next.js application.

Pages
A page is UI that is unique to a route. You can define pages by exporting a component from a page.js file. Use nested folders to define a route and a page.js file to make the route publicly accessible.

Create your first page by adding a page.js file inside the app directory:

Page File
app/page.js
// `app/page.js` is the UI for the root `/` URL
export default function Page() {
 return Hello, Next.js!
===============

;
}
Good to know:

A page is always the leaf of the route subtree.
.js, .jsx, or .tsx file extensions can be used for Pages.
A page.js file is required to make a route segment publicly accessible.
Pages are Server Components by default but can be set to a Client Component.
Pages can fetch data. View the Data Fetching section for more information.
Layouts
A layout is UI that is shared between multiple pages. On navigation, layouts preserve state, remain interactive, and do not re-render. Layouts can also be nested.

You can define a layout by default exporting a React component from a layout.js file. The component should accept a children prop that will be populated with a child layout (if it exists) or a child page during rendering.

Layout File
app/dashboard/layout.tsx
export default function DashboardLayout({
 children, // will be a page or nested layout
}: {
 children: React.ReactNode,
}) {
 return (
 
 {/\* Include shared UI here e.g. a header or sidebar \*/}
 

 {children}
 
 );
}
Good to know:

The top-most layout is called the Root Layout. This required layout is shared across all pages in an application. Root layouts must contain html and body tags.
Any route segment can optionally define its own Layout. These layouts will be shared across all pages in that segment.
Layouts in a route are nested by default. Each parent layout wraps child layouts below it using the React children prop.
You can use Route Groups to opt specific route segments in and out of shared layouts.
Layouts are Server Components by default but can be set to a Client Component.
Layouts can fetch data. View the Data Fetching section for more information.
Passing data between a parent layout and its children is not possible. However, you can fetch the same data in a route more than once, and React will automatically dedupe the requests without affecting performance.
.js, .jsx, or .tsx file extensions can be used for Layouts.
A layout.js and page.js file can be defined in the same folder. The layout will wrap the page.
Root Layout (Required)
The root layout is defined at the top level of the app directory and applies to all routes. This layout enables you to modify the initial HTML returned from the server.

app/layout.tsx
export default function RootLayout({ children }: {
 children: React.ReactNode;
}) {
 return (
 
 {children}
 
 );
}
Good to know:

The app directory must include a root layout.
The root layout must define and tags since Next.js does not automatically create them.
You can use the built-in SEO support to manage HTML elements, for example, the element.
You can use route groups to create multiple root layouts. See an example here.
The root layout is a Server Component by default and can not be set to a Client Component.
Migrating from the pages directory: The root layout replaces the \_app.js and \_document.js files. View the migration guide.

Nesting Layouts
Layouts defined inside a folder (e.g. app/dashboard/layout.js) apply to specific route segments (e.g. acme.com/dashboard) and render when those segments are active. By default, layouts in the file hierarchy are nested, which means they wrap child layouts via their children prop.

Nested Layout
app/dashboard/layout.tsx
export default function DashboardLayout({
 children,
}: {
 children: React.ReactNode,
}) {
 return <section>{children}</section>;
}
If you were to combine the two layouts above, the root layout (app/layout.js) would wrap the dashboard layout (app/dashboard/layout.js), which would wrap route segments inside app/dashboard/\*.

The two layouts would be nested as such:

Nested Layouts UI
You can use Route Groups to opt specific route segments in and out of shared layouts.

Templates
Templates are similar to layouts in that they wrap each child layout or page. Unlike layouts that persist across routes and maintain state, templates create a new instance for each of their children on navigation. This means that when a user navigates between routes that share a template, a new instance of the component is mounted, DOM elements are recreated, state is not preserved, and effects are re-synchronized.

There may be cases where you need those specific behaviors, and templates would be a more suitable option than layouts. For example:

Enter/exit animations using CSS or animation libraries.
Features that rely on useEffect (e.g logging page views) and useState (e.g a per-page feedback form).
To change the default framework behavior. For example, Suspense Boundaries inside layouts only show the fallback the first time the Layout is loaded and not when switching pages. For templates, the fallback is shown on each navigation.
Recommendation: We recommend using Layouts unless you have a specific reason to use Template.

A template can be defined by exporting a default React component from a template.js file. The component should accept a children prop which will be nested segments.

Template File
app/template.tsx
export default function Template({ children }: {
 children: React.ReactNode
}) {
 return <div>{children}</div>;
}
The rendered output of a route segment with a layout and a template will be as such:

Output
<Layout>
 {/\* Note that the template is given a unique key. \*/}
 <Template key={routeParam}>{children}</Template>
</Layout>
Modifying <head>
In the app directory, you can modify the <head> HTML elements such as title and meta using the built-in SEO support:

app/page.tsx
export const metadata = {
 title: 'Next.js'
};

export default function Page() {
 return '...'
}
Alternatively, you can use generateMetadata to fetch metadata that requires dynamic values.

app/page.tsx
export async function generateMetadata({ params, searchParams }) {
 return { title: 'Next.js' };
}

export default function Page() {
 return '...'
}
Learn more about available metadata options in the API reference.

Here is a recipe for Instant Pot Egg Bites that are high in protein, low in carbohydrates, and slow down blood glucose spikes. This recipe is also vegetarian-friendly and diabetic-friendly.

Ingredients:

* 6 eggs
* 1/2 cup cottage cheese
* 1/2 cup shredded mozzarella cheese
* 2 cups spinach, chopped
* 1/2 teaspoon salt
* 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
* 1/4 cup flax meal

Instructions:

1. Crack the eggs into a large mixing bowl and whisk them together.
2. Add the cottage cheese, shredded mozzarella, chopped spinach, salt, black pepper, and flax meal to the mixing bowl. Mix everything together until well combined.
3. Grease a silicone egg bite mold with non-stick spray or olive oil.
4. Pour the egg mixture evenly into the molds, filling each one about 3/4 full.
5. Add 1 cup of water to the Instant Pot and place the egg mold on top of the trivet.
6. Close the lid and set the Instant Pot to cook on high pressure for 8 minutes.
7. Once the timer goes off, let the pressure release naturally for 5 minutes before opening the valve to release any remaining pressure.
8. Remove the egg bites from the Instant Pot and let them cool for a few minutes before serving.

This recipe includes ingredients that are high in protein and fiber, which can help slow down blood glucose spikes. You can also try substituting the flax meal with oat fiber, as it is also high in fiber and can help reduce the glycemic load of the egg bites. Additionally, you can add other healthy vegetarian ingredients like diced bell peppers, chopped mushrooms, or diced onions to increase the fiber and protein content of the recipe.

Profilométrie robotisée
=======================

Projet réalisé dans le cadre d'une UV projet à l'IMT Nord Europe qui consiste à scanner une pièce en 3D avec un robot Kuka et un profilomètre Keyence. Le but étant de détecter de potentielles imperfections sur des pièces imprimées en 3D.

A terme, tout doit passer par python : commande des mouvements du robot, démarrage des mesures et récupérations des données du profilomètre, assemblage des données et reconstitution d'un modèle 3D, détection des défauts, etc. Nous avons donc besoin de plusieurs briques de programme élémentaires, à commencer par des API de communication avec le robot et le profilomètre.

Table des matières
------------------

- [API Kuka](#api-kuka)
- [API Profilomètre](#api-profilomètre)

API Kuka
--------

Le robot Kuka reçoit les commandes envoyées depuis python grâce à une communication série. Côté robot, un programme KRL lit les données reçues sur le port série, les interprète, et effectue les mouvements demandés. Côté python, le fichier `pykuka.py` contient toutes les fonctions nécessaires à l'utilisateur pour envoyer des commandes au robot. Ce fichier pourra ensuite être importé dans le scipt principal.

La fonction `read\_3964R\_pose` est à utiliser lorsque la fonction `SEND` est appelée dans le programme du robot. Elle sert à récupérer et décoder la position renvoyée par le robot.
La fonction `send\_3964R\_single\_char` est à utiliser lorsque la fonction `READ\_CHAR` est appelée dans le programme du robot. Elle sert à envoyer un caractère au robot.
La fonction `send\_3964R\_single\_double` est à utiliser lorsque la fonction `READ\_DOUBLE` est appelée dans le programme du robot. Elle sert à envoyer un nombre décimal au robot.
La fonction `go\_to\_pose` est à utiliser uniquement si le programme `PC2KUKA`, qui permet d'interpréter des commandes de mouvement, tourne sur le robot. Elle sert à envoyer au robot l'ordre d'atteindre une position.
La fonction `get\_pose` est à utiliser uniquement si le programme `PC2KUKA`, qui permet d'interpréter et de répondre à des commandes, tourne sur le robot. Elle sert à demander au robot d'envoyer sa position actuelle.

Ce fichier et ces fonctions peuvent être réutilisées dans d'autres projets utilisant un robot KUKA.

Utilisation du profilomètre
---------------------------

Voici quelques points importants pour comprendre le fonctionnement du profilomètre :

Le logiciel `LJ Navigator` permet de configurer le profilomètre, d'afficher et d'enregistrer des profils.
Un profil est une ligne prise par le laser du profilomètre. Sur ce modèle de profilomètre, une ligne fait 800 points. Chaque point correspond à une abscisse (x) et à une hauteur (z) mesurée par le profilomètre.
Un bouton `Démarrer affichage` permet d'afficher ce que le profilomètre voit. Le logiciel affiche alors la même chose que l'écran du profilomètre.
Un lot de profils (batch) est une suite de plusieurs profils individuels. La pièce se déplace devant le profilomètre lors de la prise des profils, transformant ainsi le nuage de point 2D d'un profil individuel à un nuage de points 3D (une coordonnée y vient donc s'ajouter). Le profilomètre dispose d'un mode batch qui réalise cette fonction.

Le profilomètre a deux modes principaux de fonctionnement :
- le mode normal qui permet de prendre des profils individuellements (voir la fonction `GetProfileAdvance` de la partie [API Profilomètre](#api-profilomètre)).
- le mode batch qui permet de faire des lots de profils. Ce mode nécéssite de choisir une fréquence d'échantillonage (fréquence à laquelle les différents profils du lot sont pris), un pas (distance entre les profils, qui dépend de la fréquence d'échantillonage et de la vitesse de la pièce sous le profilomètre) et un nombre maximal de profils à prendre. En mode batch, un enregistrement doit être déclenché (bouton `démarrer lot`, fonction `StartMeasure`), puis arrêté manuellement (bouton `arrêter lot`, fonction `StartMeasure`) ou automatiqument (lorsque le nombre de profils demandé est atteint). Attention, en mode batch, l'affichage n'est actif que pendant l'enregistrement, que ce soit sur l'écran du profilomètre ou sur le logiciel. Pendant l'enregistrement, des profils sont pris en lot, puis peuvent être enregistrés (fonction `GetBatchProfileAdvance`). Plusieurs modes d'acquisition sont possibles pour les lots :
 - le mode continu, qui prend des profils à intervalles réguliers avec une fréquence donnée, mais qui nécéssite d'avoir une vitesse de la pièce parfaitement connue pour la reconstituer proprement en 3D. C'est ce mode qui sera utilisé avec le robot.
 - le mode trigger, qui permet de déclencher la prise de chaque profil manuellement (fonction `Trigger`).
 - le mode codeur, qui permet de déclencher la prise de chaque prodil sur les changements du codeur incrémental externe qui peut être branché au profilomètre. Ceci est utile si c'est un axe linéaire muni d'un codeur qui fait bouger la pièce devant le profilomètre.

Tous ces paramètres (mode batch, fréquence, pas, nombre de profils) peuvent être régler grâce au bouton `réglage direct`.

API Profilomètre
----------------

La communication avec le profilomètre s'effectue grâce à au fichier `LJV7\_IF.dll` fourni par Keyence. Ce type de DLL étant habituellement prévu pour être utilisé dans des langages bas niveau comme le C ou le C++, un fichier `pyprofilo.py` permettra de simplifier les appels aux fonctions du DLL en s'y interfaçant grâce au module `ctypes`. Ce dernier permet de travailler avec tous les types du langage C en python, de charger des fichiers DLL, et d'appeler les fonctions qui s'y trouvent, après un travail de convertion de types, de gestion de structures C, etc. Ce fichier pourra ensuite être importé dans le scipt principal.

Transformations 3D
------------------

Le fichier `transformations.py` contient des fonctions permettant de faire des changements de base en robotique. Des matrices de transformations homogènes sont utilisées.

La fonction `get\_htm` permet de calculer une matrice de transformation homogène à partir à partir de 6 paramètres x, y, z, a, b, c qui représentent la position et l'orientation d'une base B dans une base A. Cette matrice permettra ensuite de convertir des points dont les coordonnées sont exprimées dans la base B aux mêmes points dont les coordonnées sont exprimées dans la base A. Cette fonction utilise des matrices `numpy`, qui peuvent être multipliées entres elles et inversées. Inverser une matrice permet de passer de la base A à B au lieu de passer de la base B à A. Multiplier des matrices entres elles permet d'enchainer les changements de base. La dernière matrice du produit correspond au premier changement de base.

La fonction `apply\_htm` prend en argument une matrice de transformation homogène et une liste de points, et applique la transformation. Les points ne peuvent en effet pas être multipliés directement à la matrice, il faut lui ajouter une 4ème coordonnée, et les exprimer sous forme de matrice colonne. Cette fonction se charge de ceci. Les points doivent être passés à la fonction sous la forme d'un tableau `numpy` de la forme [[x, y, z], [x, y, z], ...].

Attention : les paramètres de rotation a, b, et c ne signifient pas toujours la même chose pour les différents modèles de robot. Pour que le projet fonctionne, il faut être sûr du calcul de la matrice de rotation. Par exemple, pour le robot utilisé, la matrice de rotation est `rotation\_matrix = Rz(a) \* Ry(b) \* Rx(c)`, c'est-à-dire qu'un point est décrit par une rotation autour de x d'angle c, puis autour de y d'angle b, puis autour de z d'angle a, puis par la translation x, y, z. D'autres conventions existent cependant, comme la convention ZYZ (`rotation\_matrix = Rz(a) \* Ry(b) \* Rz(c)`). Cette expression, qui se trouve dans la fonction `get\_htm`, est donc à modifier en fonction du robot utilisé, et à déterminer à partir de sa documentation ou en faisant différents essais. Pour savoir si la matrice est correcte, suivre ce protocole :
- Créer une nouvelle base dans le robot avec une position et une orientation aléatoire.
- Relever les paramètres x, y, z, a, b, c de cette base, et les utiliser pour créer une matrice de transformation homogène avec `get\_htm`. Cette matrice permettra donc de passer des coordonnées de cette base aux coordonnées de la base world du robot.
- Emmener l'outil à une position et une orientation aléatoire.
- Affichier sur le robot et relever les coordonnées x, y, z de ce point dans la base nouvellement créée, et les exprimer dans la base world grâce à la fonction `apply\_htm`.
- Afficher sur le robot les coordonnées de ce même point, mais dans la base world (base principale, base 0) et comparer avec les résultats obtenus. Si tout correspond, alors la matrice de rotation est juste. Sinon, en tester une autre.

Protocole de calibration
------------------------

La reconstitution du scan 3D à partir des différents profils repose sur le fait que la base "profilometre" du robot soit parfaitement alignée avec la base du nuage de points renvoyé par le profilomètre. En effet, si les points renvoyés par le profilomètre peuvent être considérés comme étant dans la base "profilometre" du robot (ce qui est le cas si les deux bases sont parfaitement alignées), alors un changement de base peut permettre d'exprimer ces points dans le repère de l'outil. La pièce scannée étant fixe dans le repère de l'outil, passer tous les profils dans la base de l'outil permet automatiquement de reconstituer la pièce. Ces changements de bases sont fait en Python grâce aux coordonnées (de l'outil pince dans le repère profilometre) renvoyés par le robot avant chaque profil.

Protocole en cas de changement de robot
---------------------------------------

Pour continuer d'utiliser le projet avec un robot différent, deux étapes sont nécéssaire :
- S'assurer que la matrice de rotation soit calculée correctement, ou modifier cette dernière. Pour cela, suivre le protocole décrit dans la partie [Transformations 3D](#transformations-3d).
- Effectuer une calibration du système en suivant le protocole de la partie [Protocole de calibration](#protocole-de-calibration)

Projet réalisé dans le cadre d'une UV projet à l'IMT Nord Europe qui consiste à scanner une pièce en 3D avec un robot Kuka et un profilomètre Keyence. Le but étant de détecter de potentielles imperfections sur des pièces imprimées en 3D.

A terme, tout doit passer par python : commande des mouvements du robot, démarrage des mesures et récupérations des données du profilomètre, assemblage des données et reconstitution d'un modèle 3D, détection des défauts, etc. Nous avons donc besoin de plusieurs briques de programme élémentaires, à commencer par des API de communication avec le robot et le profilomètre.

* [API Profilomètre](#api-profilom%C3%A8tre)

API Kuka
--------

Le robot Kuka reçoit les commandes envoyées depuis python grâce à une communication série. Côté robot, un programme KRL lit les données reçues sur le port série, les interprète, et effectue les mouvements demandés. Côté python, le fichier `pykuka.py` contient toutes les fonctions nécessaires à l'utilisateur pour envoyer des commandes au robot. Ce fichier pourra ensuite être importé dans le scipt principal.

La fonction `read_3964R_pose` est à utiliser lorsque la fonction `SEND` est appelée dans le programme du robot. Elle sert à récupérer et décoder la position renvoyée par le robot.
La fonction `send_3964R_single_char` est à utiliser lorsque la fonction `READ_CHAR` est appelée dans le programme du robot. Elle sert à envoyer un caractère au robot.
La fonction `send_3964R_single_double` est à utiliser lorsque la fonction `READ_DOUBLE` est appelée dans le programme du robot. Elle sert à envoyer un nombre décimal au robot.
La fonction `go_to_pose` est à utiliser uniquement si le programme `PC2KUKA`, qui permet d'interpréter des commandes de mouvement, tourne sur le robot. Elle sert à envoyer au robot l'ordre d'atteindre une position.
La fonction `get_pose` est à utiliser uniquement si le programme `PC2KUKA`, qui permet d'interpréter et de répondre à des commandes, tourne sur le robot. Elle sert à demander au robot d'envoyer sa position actuelle.

Ce fichier et ces fonctions peuvent être réutilisées dans d'autres projets utilisant un robot KUKA.

API Profilomètre
----------------

La communication avec le profilomètre s'effectue grâce au fichier `LJV7_IF.dll` fourni par Keyence. Ce type de DLL étant habituellement prévu pour être utilisé dans des langages bas niveau comme le C ou le C++, un fichier `pyprofilo.py` permettra de simplifier les appels aux fonctions du DLL en s'y interfaçant grâce au module `ctypes`. Ce dernier permet de travailler avec tous les types du langage C en python, de charger des fichiers DLL, et d'appeler les fonctions qui s'y trou

Utilisation du profilomètre Keyence LJ-V7080 avec le logiciel LJ Navigator
==========================================================================

Le profilomètre Keyence LJ-V7080 est un appareil de mesure sans contact permettant de réaliser des mesures de profil en 3D avec une grande précision. Pour utiliser cet appareil, il est nécessaire d'utiliser le logiciel LJ Navigator, fourni avec le profilomètre.

Configuration du profilomètre
-----------------------------

Avant de pouvoir réaliser des mesures, il est nécessaire de configurer le profilomètre à l'aide du logiciel LJ Navigator. Voici les étapes à suivre :

1. Connectez le profilomètre à votre ordinateur à l'aide d'un câble USB.
2. Lancez le logiciel LJ Navigator.
3. Cliquez sur le bouton "Connect" pour connecter le profilomètre à l'ordinateur.
4. Sélectionnez le profilomètre dans la liste déroulante.
5. Cliquez sur le bouton "Settings" pour accéder aux paramètres de configuration.
6. Dans l'onglet "General", configurez les paramètres généraux du profilomètre, tels que la langue, le format de date et d'heure, etc.
7. Dans l'onglet "Measurement", configurez les paramètres de mesure du profilomètre. Vous pouvez notamment définir la distance de mesure, la vitesse de déplacement de la pièce à mesurer, la fréquence d'échantillonnage, etc.
8. Dans l'onglet "Batch", configurez les paramètres de mesure en mode batch. Vous pouvez notamment définir la fréquence d'échantillonnage, le nombre de profils à mesurer, etc.
9. Dans l'onglet "Data", configurez les paramètres d'enregistrement des données de mesure. Vous pouvez notamment définir le format de fichier de sortie, le dossier de destination, etc.
10. Cliquez sur le bouton "Save" pour enregistrer les paramètres de configuration.

Mesure avec le profilomètre
---------------------------

Une fois le profilomètre configuré, vous pouvez procéder à la mesure de la pièce à l'aide du logiciel LJ Navigator. Voici les étapes à suivre :

1. Placez la pièce à mesurer sous le profilomètre.
2. Dans le logiciel LJ Navigator, cliquez sur le bouton "Start Display" pour afficher l'image capturée par le profilomètre.
3. Cliquez sur le bouton "Start Batch" pour démarrer la mesure en mode batch. Le profilomètre commencera alors à prendre des mesures en suivant les paramètres de configuration définis précédemment.
4. Lorsque la mesure est terminée, cliquez sur le bouton "Stop Batch" pour arrêter la prise de mesure.
5. Vous pouvez alors enregistrer les données de mesure en cliquant sur le bouton "Save". Les données seront enregistrées dans le dossier de destination défini dans les paramètres de configuration.

Analyse des données de mesure
-----------------------------

Une fois les données de mesure enregistrées, vous pouvez les analyser à l'aide du logiciel LJ Navigator ou d'un logiciel de traitement de données tel que MATLAB ou Python. Les données de mesure sont enregistrées au format CSV, ce qui facilite leur traitement.

Il est également possible de visualiser les données de mesure en 3D à l'aide de logiciels de modélisation tels que MeshLab

Other Changes

# Fixed Asset Accounting - Design
### Glossary 
\*\*\*GL\*\* : The Amazon General Ledger for tracking all accounting events in Amazon businesses.\*
\*\*AFFS\*\* : Amazon Financial Foundation Services earlier known as eCFI which owns USL, Flash, Flare etc.
\*\*\*USL or Unified Subledger\*\* : It is a subledger owned by AFFS, which batches the events hourly and sends them to GL for multiple businesses such as prime, retail, alexa etc.\*
\*\*\*CBE or Canonical business event\*\*: This is payload format for events sent to USL.\*
\*\*\*COA or Chart of Accounts\*\* : Also known otherwise as GL\_Segments data which needs to present for all data sent to GL. The 7 segments are company\_code, location, account, cost\_center, project, channel and product.\*
\*\*\*Flash or Financial Ledger and Accounting Systems Hub\*\*: Central Platform owned by AFFS team for onboarding businesses and integrating with them to send updates to GL\*
\*\*\*Flare\*\*: It is a multi-tenant rules authoring and execution engine. Flare is more than a configuration store. Flare serves as a platform that can manage the entire lifecycle of our business rules.\*
\*\*\*SAFE or Simplified Accounting and Folio Engine\*\* : It is a push based audit trail recording system under AFFS which collects all business activities that occur in a system, batch them and persist in the respective business owned S3 account.\*
\*\*\*GTID or Global Transaction ID\*\*: It is used to track events in the AFFS workflows and pipelines until sent to USL\*
\*\*\*Source2USL\*\* : It was created by AFFS to generate reconciliation reports for all clients publishing data to USL via Flash.\*
\*\*Double entry accounting :\*\* It is a method of [bookkeeping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bookkeeping) that relies on a two-sided [accounting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accounting) entry to maintain financial information

### GL Integration Proposal
[Spursh](https://w.amazon.com/bin/view/FinTech/GeneralLedger/Spursh/JournalIntegrationPlatform) is the central system owned by Close team which ingest JEs (Journal Entries) from various upstream sources and publishes them to OFA-GL in ~~a~~ batches. They allow both automated and manual JE ingestion processes. [USL](https://w.amazon.com/bin/view/AFFS-Home/AFFS-Help/USL/) is one such source for Spursh where it has automated sending JEs to Spursh for various Amazon businesses including retail ordering. [Teller](https://w.amazon.com/bin/view/Main/Teller/), which is the new AP subledger, also uses USL to publish entries to Spursh and subsequently to GL. [Project Amigos](https://w.amazon.com/bin/view/Bill2Pay/Bill2Pay\_Tech\_Vision/) is a similar initiative where they are migrating away from OFA-AR subledger using USL. After going through all the documentation and talking to engineers in the AP, AR domain, we concluded that we could use their learnings and not send JEs to Spursh as an independent source system, and rather send it via USL like Teller and Cimmaron (Amigos). Apart from this there are some other advantages of being part of the USL ecosystem:
1. USL is an Amazon scale solution already processing thousands of transactions per second across multiple geographies and businesses.
2. Newer subledgers onboarding to USL while moving away from OFA can establish a standard workflow for all Subledger to GL interactions thus creating reusable workflows.
3. USL has in built checks and balances to help with validations across different tenants.
4. USL has other tools in its ecosystem which we can leverage (i.e Source2USL for reconciliation)
5. event-based interfaces
Thus, we have decided to go ahead with USL integration for FASL and thus onboarding to Flash which is a pre-requisite for sending data to USL. We would be sending CBE messages to a system called FLARE which would then subsequently publish it to USL. More on how the various components in USL ecosystem communicate with each other can be found [here](https://w.amazon.com/bin/view/AFFS-Home/AFFS-Help/FLASH-Onboarding-Overview/FLASH-Systems/).

#### \*\*Source Systems\*\*
There will be two services sending asset events to the accounting generator. \*\*Asset Service\*\* will be responsible for sending asset create, update, transfer and retire events while \*\*Depreciation Service\*\* will be sending asset depreciation events. 
\*\*\*Asset Service would be sending \_one-off events\_ while depreciation events may be sent in \_batches.\_\*


#### \*\*Asset Accounting Systems\*\*
This comprises of three sub-systems: \*\*Accounting Generator\*\*, \*\*Accounting Reconciliation\*\* and \*\*Accounting Publisher\*\*.
\*\*Accounting Generator\*\* creates a multi-step workflow for each asset event received from the upstream source systems. It transforms the asset event to a CBE, then enriches the event with a GTID by calling reconciliation and then sends it to publisher for sending it to Flash. It also is responsible for state management along with error handling.
\*\*Accounting Reconciliation\*\* enriches CBE events with GTID by calling SAFE to generate unique id for each event. GTID is essential for tracking CBE events inside the Flash systems. The GTID is then used for viewing the event status as well as for reconciliation and reporting for our users.
\*\*Accounting Publisher\*\* sends CBE events to Flash booking service and keeps track of the responses received from Flash along with retry capability for retryable errors (i.e 5XX)


#### Flash/USL Services
AFFS has a suite of services including Flash, Flare, SAFE, Source2USL and USL. 
\*\*Flash\*\* interacts with upstream source systems which send CBEs. It spawns herd workflows to send the event through multiple services before sending it to USL.
\*\*Flare\*\* is the multi-tenant config store which is used by source systems to add business use-case specific metadata in the CBE such as \*business\_namespace, financial\_component\* etc. We would be creating our own model configs for parsing our CBE events.
\*\*SAFE\*\* is a centralized uuid generator for the CBE events as it generates GTID for each CBE by using folio\_id, sequence\_id and timestamp data. Before SAFE, each source system had to create its own uuid generator to create and track the GTIDs.
\*\*Source2USL\*\* helps in generating month close reconciliation reports for the source systems and also provides a dashboard for tracking the events with the help of GTID.
\*\*USL\*\* aggregates CBE events received from all sources including fixed assets and sends them to Spursh for publishing to GL.

### Low Level Design 
#### Services Infrastructure
For each of our components we have to select the compute and storage platform and for orchestrating the data flow we need an orchestration platform with state management capabilities. 
\*\*Orchestration Options: 
\*\*
AWS Step functions is the obvious choice to use for our orchestration needs as its other options such as SWF have unofficially been deprecated by not being supported in CDK. (It is also available in 2 CN regions )


>\*Orchestration centrally manages a workflow by breaking it into multiple steps, adding flow logic, and tracking the inputs and outputs between the steps. As your applications run, Step Functions maintains the application state, tracking exactly which workflow step your application is in, and stores an event log of data that is passed between application components. That means if the workflow is interrupted for any reason, your application can pick up right where it left off.\*


Even within step functions, we have 2 types a)Standard b)Express. We would be using the standard workflow in our case and some of the reasoning behind that has been addressed in the FAQ. 
\*\*Compute Options: 
\*\*
Step Functions has support for all three of our possible compute choices: Lambda, ECS Fargate and Batch. For our synchronous and stateless APIs, lambda would be the better lightweight compute choice (i.e Publisher) but for other apis which are asynchronous or do state management we would need to look at other compute options such as fargate and batch which are very equivalent cost wise as well.


|Dimension |Lambda (preferred) |Batch |ECS Fargate |
|--- |--- |--- |--- |
|Startup Latency |Cold start delays |Instance startup time with image load |Always up |
|Memory and Runtime |Runtime: 15 minutes
Memory:128MB to 10 GB |Fully configurable and no runtime limits except job timeouts can be explicitly set |Fully configurable and no runtime limits |
|Batch Support |Scales to batch use case with parallel invocations |Best bit for batch requests |Can support batch |
|Sync/Async |Async |Async |Supports both hence can support UI as well |

\*\*\*The only concern with Lambda which can push us towards ECS fargate would be the UI use case latency requirements.\*

#### API Definitions
We will be hosting 3 primary APIs using AWI gateways and backed with Lambda and step functions
1. \*\*submitAssetAccountingEvent\*\*(Request:AssetEventPayload, Response: ExecutionID) : This is the primary API for the accounting service. It would trigger a step function workflow for each request and respond with an executionID to the client. It would be composed of a 3-step workflow of lambdas: a)Transformer b)Enrichment c)Publisher. Each one of them would update the event status table in Dynamo based on their success/failures. (Optional: We can add support for batch mode as well)
[Image: FASL\_Accounting-Page-5(1).png]
1. \*\*getAssetAccountingEventStatus\*\*(Request: ExecutionID, Response: StatusEnum) : This is the get api to provide clients ability to track the state of their submitted asset events. (i.e published to USL or failed). We will use the step function executionIDs as our global event tracking keys since they are also automatically tracked in step function execution history for 90 days. We would look up the event progress and status using this executionID in our dynamo state table and respond with the last known status.


[Image: FASL\_Accounting-Page-5(2).png]


1. \*\*generateReconReport\*\*(Request: , Response: List): This would be triggered for reconciliation reporting either by a customer or via a cron/eventbridge rule. This would then call source2USL to get recon status of all FAA events in the specified time interval. (Optional : We can also cache the requests on our end in case of duplicate requests.)

### Failure Scenarios
1. Upstream malformed asset data : Non-retryable and should return validation errors to the source systems
2. API Gateway failed to invoke step functions : Clients would get an error message and should retry requests after some time.
3. Idempotency errors : Flash has built-in support for idempotence by using idempotence\_id and GTID in our downstream flow, but there can be idempotency concerns from our upstream sources. For instance, clients such as depreciation engine can retry requests thus sending duplicate events to us, which if not addressed will result in duplicate entries in GL. Some of the risks here can be mitigated by enforcing an idempotency\_key in our API but we would need to make sure that it does not in any way create inaccurate costs or balances for the asset.
4. Flash publish failed: There can be multiple errors leading to publish errors and we would need to have handlers for the specific error codes (i.e 5XX errors can be retried and malformed data errors would need to be just logged with exception)
5. USL reconciliation failure: Some of asset events published to Flash may fail to reconcile with the source asset events. We would need to have daily/hourly reporting of these errors and a redrive mechanism.
6. SAFE server side errors: In this case, we can have exponential retry with backoff as it is essential to get the GTID before publishing the CBE to Flash.

En este caso, te recomiendo utilizar un contenedor Docker para ejecutar el comando `az artifacts universal publish` en un entorno que tenga una versión compatible de la biblioteca libssl.

Puedes seguir estos pasos para crear un contenedor Docker:

1. Crea un archivo `Dockerfile` en un directorio vacío con el siguiente contenido:
```sql
FROM ubuntu:20.04

RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y curl gnupg lsb-release && \
    curl -sL https://packages.microsoft.com/keys/microsoft.asc | gpg --dearmor | tee /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/microsoft.gpg > /dev/null && \
    echo "deb [arch=amd64] https://packages.microsoft.com/repos/azure-cli/ $(lsb_release -cs) main" | tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/azure-cli.list && \
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y azure-cli
```
Este Dockerfile crea un contenedor basado en Ubuntu 20.04 e instala Azure CLI en él.

1. Construye la imagen del contenedor ejecutando este comando en el mismo directorio que el Dockerfile:
```
docker build -t azure-cli-ubuntu20.04 .
```
1. Ejecuta un contenedor con la imagen creada y monta tu directorio actual en el contenedor:
```bash
docker run -it --rm -v "$(pwd):/workspace" -w /workspace azure-cli-ubuntu20.04
```
Ahora estarás dentro del contenedor Docker con un entorno Ubuntu 20.04 y tendrás acceso a la CLI de Azure.

1. Autentícate en Azure ejecutando `az login` y sigue las instrucciones proporcionadas.
2. Ejecuta el comando `az artifacts universal publish` dentro del contenedor, proporcionando los argumentos necesarios.

Una vez que hayas terminado de trabajar con el contenedor, simplemente escribe `exit` para salir y eliminar el contenedor. Ten en cuenta que los cambios realizados dentro del contenedor no se guardarán, a excepción de los archivos en el directorio montado (`/workspace` en este caso).

(인스타그램 배너 광고를 통해 얻는 혜택)

3. Instagram의 광범위한 타겟팅 옵션에 액세스합니다.
유튜브 광고
(YouTube 광고 집행 시 타겟팅)

(YouTube 광고 광고 전략)

(YouTube 광고를 통해 얻는 혜택)

3. 유료 시청 모델을 통한 비용 효율적인 광고.
추천 매체별로 이러한 맞춤형 광고 전략을 구현함으로써 Sand Workshop은 잠재 고객을 효과적으로 타겟팅하고 브랜드 인지도를 높이며 판매를 촉진할 수 있습니다. 각 매체는 광고 성과를 최적화할 수 있는 고유한 이점과 기회를 제공하여 브랜드가 마케팅 목표를 달성하도록 돕습니다.

为什么chrome插件提交多语言版本后，审核通过会变慢
Chrome插件的多语言版本审核速度变慢可能有多种原因，下面列举一些可能的原因：

1. 提交多语言版本后，插件的文件数量和大小会增加，可能会增加审核的工作量和时间。
2. 如果您在多语言版本中包含了一些新的功能或更新了旧的功能，这可能需要审核人员更多的时间来测试和确认插件的稳定性和安全性。
3. 如果您的插件使用了一些第三方库或API，审核人员需要花费更多的时间来确认这些库和API的安全性和合规性，以确保它们不会损害用户的隐私和安全。
4. 审核人员可能会更加谨慎地审核多语言版本，因为这些版本可能需要考虑更多的地区和语言，可能会涉及到一些文化和法律上的差异。

综上所述，Chrome插件提交多语言版本后审核时间变慢可能是由于多种原因造成的。如果您遇到了审核时间变慢的问题，可以通过Chrome Web Store的开发者支持来获得更多帮助和指导。

上海市第三中级人民法院
刑事判决书
案号：（2023）沪03刑初2号
被告人林宗强，男，1963年1月26日生，公民身份号码XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX，XX，文盲，系“8号中巴船”船员，住福建省连江县；因涉嫌犯走私普通货物罪于2022年9月27日被刑事拘留，同日被取保候审，同年10月31日被继续取保候审，2023年2月8日被逮捕。现羁押于上海市静安区看守所（北）。
辩护人钱昌杰，上海市大公律师事务所律师。
上海市人民检察院第三分院以沪检三分刑诉〔2023〕1号起诉书指控被告人林宗强犯走私普通货物罪，于2023年1月3日向本院提起公诉。本院于次日立案并依法组成合议庭，通知上海市法律援助中心指派律师为被告人林宗强提供辩护，公开开庭审理了本案。上海市人民检察院第三分院指派检察员刘阿华出庭支持公诉。被告人林宗强及其辩护人钱昌杰到庭参加诉讼。现已审理终结。
上海市人民检察院第三分院起诉指控，2019年4月至2020年7月间，被告人林宗强为牟取非法利益，明知薛某、庄某2（均另案处理）等人从事走私成品油活动，仍出资入股“8号中巴船”，多次与他人共同驾乘“8号中巴船”前往我国领海外水域接驳成品油入境。2020年7月11日1时许，“8号中巴船”在长江口水域向两艘“小巴船”过驳成品油后，两艘“小巴船”被公安机关查获。经上海吴淞海关计核，被告人林宗强采用上述方式参与“8号中巴船”走私成品油18票，偷逃应缴税额共计人民币（以下币种均为人民币）37,792,958.96元。
2022年9月27日，被告人林宗强被公安机关抓获，到案后如实供述了上述犯罪事实。
为支持上述指控事实，公诉机关出示了侦查机关提供、制作、调取的《受案登记表》《立案决定书》《到案经过》《扣押决定书》《扣押清单》《扣押笔录》《银行流水记录》《股本单》《坐标轨迹图》《核税说明》《户籍证明》，上海吴淞海关出具的《涉嫌走私的货物、物品偷逃税款海关核定证明书》，证人庄某证言，另案处理人员庄某2、吴某、高某、张某、王某等人的供述以及被告人林宗强的供述等证据，认为被告人林宗强为牟取非法利益，经与他人共谋，违反海关法规，逃避海关监管，出资入股并与他人共同驾驶船只前往我国领海外接驳成品油后绕关走私入境，偷逃应缴税额达3,779万余元，偷逃应缴税额特别巨大，其行为触犯了《中华人民共和国刑法》第一百五十三条第一款第（三）项、第三款之规定，应当以走私普通货物罪追究其刑事责任。在共同犯罪中，被告人林宗强起次要作用，根据《中华人民共和国刑法》第二十五条第一款、第二十七条的规定，系从犯，应当从轻或者减轻处罚。被告人林宗强到案后能如实供述自己的罪行，根据《中华人民共和国刑法》第六十七条第三款的规定，可以从轻处罚。据此，提请本院依法审判。
被告人林宗强对起诉指控的犯罪事实供认不讳并自愿认罪，请求法庭对其从宽处罚并适用缓刑。
林宗强的辩护人对起诉指控林宗强构成走私普通货物罪无异议，提出林宗强无前科，犯罪的主观恶性较小；其到案后始终如实供述自己的罪行，认罪态度好；其在共同犯罪中起次要作用，系从犯，依法应当减轻处罚；其愿意退缴违法所得，悔罪态度好，对其适用缓刑对所在社区无不良影响，请求法庭对其减轻处罚并适用缓刑。
经审理查明，2019年4月至2020年7月间，被告人林宗强为牟取非法利益，在明知薛某、庄某2（均另案处理）等人从事走私成品油活动的情况下，仍出资入股“8号中巴船”并获取工资，同时担任船员与他人共同驾乘“8号中巴船”多次前往我国领海外水域接驳成品油入境。2020年7月11日1时许，被告人林宗强等人驾驶“8号中巴船”在长江口水域将自境外接驳的成品油过驳至“皖舒城货0556”“信通16号”两艘小巴船，随后，上述两艘小巴船先后被上海市公安局港航公安局拦截，船上成品油被当场查获。经上海吴淞海关计核，被告人林宗强采用上述方式参与“8号中巴船”走私成品油18票，偷逃应缴税额共计37,792,958.96元。
2022年9月27日，被告人林宗强被公安机关抓获，到案后如实供述了上述犯罪事实。
上述事实，有下列公诉机关提供的、经控辩双方当庭质证、法庭查证属实的证据予以证实，本院予以确认：
1.侦查机关出具的《受案登记表》《立案决定书》《到案经过》等书证，与被告人林宗强的供述相互印证，证实本案的案发经过及被告人林宗强的到案经过等事实。
2.侦查机关制作的《扣押决定书》《扣押清单》《扣押笔录》等书证，证实涉案物品被依法扣押的事实。
3.侦查机关调取的《银行流水记录》《股本单》及制作的《坐标轨迹图》等书证，另案处理人员庄某2、吴某、高某、张某、王某等人的供述，证人庄某证言，与被告人林宗强的供述相互印证，证实被告人林宗强入股薛某走私成品油团伙并在“8号中巴船”上担任船员，自2019年起多次前往我国领海外水域接驳成品油后绕关走私入境并获取工资等事实。
4.上海吴淞海关出具的《涉嫌走私的货物、物品偷逃税款海关核定证明书》、侦查机关的《核税说明》，证实涉案成品油的实际成交价格及偷逃应缴税额的事实。
5.侦查机关调取的《户籍证明》与被告人林宗强的供述相互印证，证实了林宗强的自然身份状况。
本院认为，被告人林宗强为牟取非法利益，经与他人共谋，违反海关法规，逃避海关监管，出资入股并与他人共同驾驶船只前往我国领海外接驳成品油后绕关走私入境，偷逃应缴税额达3,779万余元，偷逃应缴税额特别巨大，其行为已构成走私普通货物罪，依法应予处罚。公诉机关起诉指控的事实清楚，证据确实、充分，罪名成立，本院予以支持。在共同犯罪中，被告人林宗强起次要作用，系从犯，依法应当从轻或者减轻处罚。被告人林宗强到案后能如实供述自己的罪行，依法可以从轻处罚。根据被告人林宗强的犯罪事实、性质、情节及认罪悔罪态度，本院决定对其减轻处罚。辩护人的相关辩护意见予以采纳。但林宗强参与犯罪次数多，持续时间长，且偷逃应缴税额特别巨大，不具备适用缓刑的条件，故对林宗强及其辩护人要求适用缓刑的意见不予采纳。据此，依照《中华人民共和国刑法》第一百五十三条第一款第（二）项、第（三）项、第三款，第二十五条第一款，第二十七条，第六十七条第三款，第五十二条，第五十三条第一款，第六十四条以及《最高人民法院、最高人民检察院关于办理走私刑事案件适用法律若干问题的解释》第十六条第一款之规定，判决如下：
一、被告人林宗强犯走私普通货物罪，判处有期徒刑三年三个月，并处罚金人民币三十万元。
（刑期从判决执行之日起计算。判决执行以前先行羁押的，羁押一日折抵刑期一日，即自2023年2月8日起至2026年5月6日止。罚金于本判决生效后一个月内一次缴纳。）
二、走私犯罪违法所得予以追缴，供犯罪所用的本人财物予以没收。
如不服本判决，可在接到判决书的第二日起十日内，通过本院或者直接向上海市高级人民法院提出上诉。书面上诉的，应当提交上诉状正本一份，副本×份。
